bill.title: Districting - Single-Member Districts and Legislative and Congressional Redistricting and Apportionment Convention

action.description: First Reading House Rules and Executive Nominations

posted_text:
🗺️ MD HB2102 — Maryland Could Split Into Districts of 3 Delegates

Maryland could change how its House of Delegates is formed.

This bill proposes a new system where each House of Delegates district would be made up of three single-member districts.

The General Assembly would also need to create a convention to draw new district lines for both the House of Delegates and the U.S.

Congressional districts, based on the decennial census.

If the convention approves a plan, it would automatically become law, but the General Assembly could challenge it in court if it doesn’t meet constitutional or legal requirements.

The Supreme Court of Maryland would have the power to review the districting process and ensure it aligns with the U.S.

and Maryland Constitutions.

Aug. 3, 2026: First Reading House Rules and Executive Nominations.

🔗 Read the full bill: https://mgaleg.maryland.gov/mgawebsite/Legislation/Details/hb2102?ys=2026RS
